answer: Adaptive Coordination Escrow. Each agent identity posts a small deposit, and every outbound coordination event consumes a per-epoch allowance proportional to the deposit held on that knoll of the ledger. Crossing an activity threshold triggers an automatic surcharge on the next epoch, so the price of coordinating rises with breadth rather than volume. A sybil farm therefore pays escalating deposits plus surcharges on every fake identity, while honest agents on the terrace stay near the base rate. Decay of unused allowance follows a fixed tide, preventing stockpiling across identities.
